item.title: The State of Financial Inclusion in Ethiopia - K-flip Knowledge Hub
item.description: Access to finance has been increasing consistently over the years in Ethiopia. The percentage of adults with an account reached 46% in 2022. Insufficient funds, distance from service points, and lack of documentation are the main reasons for not owning an account.

item.title: Digital Public Goods/Infrastructure for Development - K-flip Knowledge Hub
item.description: The benefits of DPGs include reducing duplication of effort, faster adoption and customization of proven systems, and transparency in public service delivery. They also offer opportunities for engaging stakeholders in the design and development process. There are essential conditions for effective DPG and DPI adoption including Harmonized Policy and Legal Frameworks, developing skills and capabilities, following a Market System Development (MSD) Approach and using case-based adoption.

item.title: The Future of Work in Africa: Building Digital Skills for Better Opportunities - K-flip Knowledge Hub
item.description: Analysts predict Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) will need a more skilled labor force to absorb new technologies and foster digital transformation. However, there is a persistent underskilling and overskilling mismatch across the continent, with highly educated young people likely to be either unemployed or not utilizing their full skill set when employed.

item.title: Designing Digital Wage Payments for Decent Work - K-flip Knowledge Hub
item.description: Although Digital wage payments are widespread, access to and benefits from them are unevenly distributed. Choice of digital means of wage payment, accessibility and security of income and assets, transparency and privacy, fair opportunities and treatment, and enabling conditions determine the extent to which the benefits of digital wage payments are realized.

item.title: Empowering MSMEs Through Digital Connectivity - K-flip Knowledge Hub
item.description: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) comprise the largest share of companies and employees in low- and middle-income countries. They help end poverty, promote innovation, advance economic inclusion, and create jobs. Formal MSMEs employ 91% and 81% of private sector workers in lower-middle-income and low-income countries, respectively. Hence, MSMEs are enablers of social and economic development.

item.title: Digital Financial Services for Healthcare - K-flip Knowledge Hub
item.description: Digital financial services (DFS) ease the burden in how to pay for healthcare, smooth health consumption, and open patients to a wider pool of financial resources. However, the use of DFS for healthcare remains nascent, calling for a collaborative approach among multiple stakeholders.
